clue.text: Dwarf fish raised, ultimately cheap and nasty

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word for fish is read from the bottom up

parts.note: eels are fish

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letters of the words cheap and nasty

explanation.surface: A complaint about shoddy, nasty fish served up somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EELS into SLEE; 'ultimately' takes P and Y from the ends of 'cheap' and 'nasty'. 'Dwarf' looks like a verb or adjective but names one of the seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy is one of the seven dwarfs in the Snow White story.

clue.text: Student broadcast erotic sound of dirty little blighters

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a student's degree

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: sound reasoning is logical reasoning

explanation.surface: A student airs something smutty about grubby little pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges EROTIC into CTERIO. 'sound' looks like a noise but is the adjective meaning valid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are tiny germs, so anything relating to them concerns those small disease-carrying organisms.

clue.text: Native's fling with a girl, according to gossip

indicators.note: gossip is talk, so the words are what someone would say out loud

parts.note: to shy is to throw or fling; Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle about a native man's brief affair with a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' looks like a romance but is the verb throw, SHY; said together, SHY ANNE matches the tribe's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Control fencing salesman, making influence up front

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the salesman's word is penned inside the word for control

parts.note: to possess is to have control of
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A man selling fencing gains early sway over a buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like the goods the salesman sells, but here it means surrounding. The definition means to influence in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepossess someone is to bias them beforehand, shaping their opinion in advance.

clue.text: At the primary stage, Bill and Ben entertained a child

indicators.note: primary means first, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: The Flowerpot Men, Bill and Ben, amused a small child in early school.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben were the Flowerpot Men of a classic British children's TV show, which suits the picture of a young child.
explanation.definitionFit: A babe is an infant or very young child.

clue.text: Eating soil regularly, spoils teeth

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the word for spoils swallows the other letters

parts.note: mars means spoils or damages

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of soil, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone who eats dirt from time to time ruins their teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of 'soil', and 'Eating' puts them inside the word for spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: Molars are the broad grinding teeth at the back of the mouth.

clue.text: On the other hand, straighten out how one could cut deal, say

definitions.text: how one could cut deal, say

parts.note: again, as in 'then again', means on the other hand

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of straighten are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to sort out a timber deal, cut properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges STRAIGHTEN into STHEGRAIN. 'deal' is the wood (pine or fir board), not a bargain; 'say' marks it as an example of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood cut across the line of its fibres is cut against them; deal is a kind of softwood.

clue.text: 16 left, parting before daughter who wasn't ready

parts.note: the answer to 16 Across is the old letter eth

indicators.note: parting means splitting apart, so the letter for left divides the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A daughter who was not prepared left before the others.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside ERE, making ELRE. The definition alludes to the English king known as 'the Unready', whose nickname actually meant badly advised.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred the Unready was an Anglo-Saxon king whose famous nickname suggested a lack of preparedness.

clue.text: Agitation about European's tanned skin

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for agitation goes round the letter

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be agitated
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European gets worked up about their suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanned skin' suggests a sunbather, but it is hide treated in a tannery.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is animal hide preserved by tanning.

clue.text: Surrounded by anxiety, suppressing a little more

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so the word for anxiety contains the shortened word

parts.note: angst is anxiety or dread

indicators.note: only a little of the word more is used, its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone holding back their worries a little more under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: A first guess may take 'a little more' as the definition; it is wordplay, and 'Surrounded by' is the definition. 'a little' keeps just the first two letters of 'more'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amongst means in the midst of, enclosed within a group.

clue.text: Lobby guard to dismiss leader

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is removed from the word for guard

parts.note: a sentry is a guard

explanation.surface: A pressure group wants to sack the head of security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby' looks like a verb about pressure groups but is a noun, the hall at a building's door.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is an entrance hall or vestibule, the same as a lobby.

clue.text: Mineral layer covered by Pascal's French city

indicators.note: covered by means enclosed within, so the word for layer sits inside the unit symbol

parts.note: Pa is the symbol for the pascal, the unit of pressure
a hen is a bird that lays eggs
cité is French for city

explanation.surface: A mineral deposit found in the French city of the philosopher Pascal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a stratum, apt for a mineral, but means an egg-laying hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenacite is a rare beryllium silicate crystal sometimes cut as a gemstone.

clue.text: Underwear discovered in Dutch litter, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the words found are matched by how they are spoken

parts.note: what is found among a Dutch litter: 'old Dutch' is London slang for a wife, and runts are the weakest of a litter, giving wife and runts

explanation.surface: Someone's pants turn up among rubbish in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is not the nationality: 'old Dutch' is London slang for a wife. Spoken quickly, WIFE RUNTS comes close to the name of the men's briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are men's briefs with an upside-down Y-shaped seam at the front.

clue.text: Half-hearted wife regularly fears one who maltreats

indicators.note: half of the heart, one of the two middle letters, is removed from the word for wife

parts.note: missus is informal for wife

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of fears, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A lukewarm wife often fears a man who mistreats her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' drops one of the two central S letters of MISSUS, leaving MISUS; 'regularly' adds ER from 'fears'.
explanation.definitionFit: A misuser treats someone or something badly or wrongly.

clue.text: Instructors somehow harass him -I should intervene

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so the letter goes in among the others
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker protests that they must step in when teachers pester someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' scrambles the nine letters of the two words, and 'should intervene' slots the I into them.
explanation.definitionFit: Maharishis are Hindu sages who teach spiritual knowledge to followers.

clue.text: Crowd went by car

definitions.meaning: a large moving mass of people or animals
past tense of the verb meaning to steer a car along

explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a herd or throng; also the past tense of operating a vehicle, travelling by motor.

clue.text: Places one's set up in termini

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, the reversed letters inside the word for termini

parts.note: depots are bus or rail termini

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised, read from the bottom

parts.note: one's is read as I'S, the letter I for one with the S of is

explanation.surface: Someone's luggage is set down at the end stations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns 'one's' (I'S) upside down in this down clue, and 'in' puts that inside the word for termini.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit is to put or lay something down somewhere, so the verb sense matches.

clue.text: Finally come out with old English letter

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A demand to finally admit to something about an old English letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come out with' reads as a phrasal verb meaning say, but only its last letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: Eth is a runic-derived character used in Old English and still in Icelandic.

clue.text: A heartless Clint Eastwood would have done it countless times

definitions.text: A heartless Clint Eastwood would have done it countless times

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle, so only the first and last letters of each name survive

explanation.surface: The tough-guy film star has played cold-blooded killers in film after film.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the star made countless films. CT and ED come from the first and last letters of 'Clint' and 'Eastwood'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clint Eastwood is a film star who has performed in movies for decades.

clue.text: Excellent food initially making brother incontinent after the break?

indicators.note: after the word incontinent is broken into two, the word for brother sits in the continent

parts.note: split as 'in continent', the continent being Asia, with in placing the other letters inside

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of making

parts.note: bro is informal for brother

explanation.surface: Fine food at first makes a brother lose control after the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks you to break 'incontinent' into 'in continent': the first letter of 'making' and the word for brother go inside that continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, so it is used for anything delicious.

clue.text: Cast lines should never catch them unawares

definitions.text: Cast lines should never catch them unawares

parts.words: Cast lines should never catch them unawares
parts.note: reads as fishing lines, but cast means actors; the reminders whispered to actors who forget lines must be quick, timely ones

explanation.surface: Anglers' lines should never surprise the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast lines' suggests fishing; it means the actors' lines, and the answer works as noun (cues) and as the idea of being punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompts are whispered cues given to actors in a theatre who forget what to say.

clue.text: Firework manufactured by favourite cockney firm

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
a cockney drops the H, so hard becomes 'ard

explanation.surface: A fireworks company run by a favourite East Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney is a working-class Londoner, whose accent drops initial H. 'firm' looks like a company but means hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A petard is a small explosive device, as in 'hoist with his own petard'.

clue.text: In vessel, birds wheeling, no sign of a cage?

indicators.note: wheeling means turning round, so the run of letters is read backwards
in means contained within, so the letters are found inside the words vessel and birds

explanation.surface: A picture of birds circling inside a ship, with no cage in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'wheeling' together pull SSELBIR out of 'vessel, birds' and turn it round. The definition is cryptic: with no ribs, there is no ribcage.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature without ribs has no ribcage, the bony frame round the chest.

clue.text: River bird with wings of eagle

parts.note: a swan is a bird

indicators.note: wings are at the two sides, so the first and last letters of eagle are taken

explanation.surface: A river bird spreads wings like an eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Swanee is the river of the Stephen Foster song 'Old Folks at Home'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swanee (Suwannee) is a river in Georgia and Florida made famous in song.

clue.text: Better to finish thus when all is lost?

definitions.text: Better to finish thus when all is lost?

parts.words: Better to finish thus when all is lost?
parts.note: a better here is a bettor, a gambler; someone who has gambled away everything is said to lose even the garment off their back

explanation.surface: A gloomy saying that it is best to end a certain way once everything is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like a comparative but is someone who bets; 'lose your shirt' means lose all your money.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler who has lost everything is left without the garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Number doesn't begin to be divisible by two

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for number is left off

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: A number that cannot start to be split into halves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like part of the maths sentence but just stands for SEVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An even number can be split into two equal whole parts with nothing left over.

clue.text: Procreate, ends having broken off sheath

indicators.note: the ends, two letters at each side, are snapped off the word procreate

explanation.surface: Breeding stops once the ends of a protective cover break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends having broken off' removes PR and TE from PROCREATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocrea is a botanical sheath round a plant stem formed from joined stipules.

clue.text: Swallow inside box, say, finds plant

indicators.note: inside places the word for swallow within the word for box

parts.note: box is an example of a tree, hence 'say'
to swallow is to eat

explanation.surface: A swallow nesting in a box finds a plant to perch on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a bird, apt with 'box', but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea tree is an Australasian shrub whose leaves give a well-known oil.

clue.text: Make rainbow-coloured flag, finally packed in a cube

indicators.note: the final letter of the flower's name is packed into the word for a cube

parts.note: a flag is a type of iris, the plant
a die is a cube used in games

explanation.surface: Someone at last stuffs a flag into a box to make it colourful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is the wild iris, not a banner. 'finally packed in' moves the flower's last letter inside the word for a cube.
explanation.definitionFit: To iridise is to make something iridescent, shimmering with many colours.
